newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH MPS PASS BILL ON PAP NEWS AGENCY SELL-OFF.
newsitem.headline: POLISH MPS PASS BILL ON PAP NEWS AGENCY SELL-OFF.

text.p: Poland's lower house of Parliament, the Sejm, on Thursday passed a bill paving the way for the sale of the national press agency PAP after transforming it into a treasury-owned joint stock company.

By a vote of 368 to 11 with three abstentions, the Sejm passed the measure, which envisages a sale of up to 49 percent of the news agency in two years after it becomes a joint-stock firm, which was expected at the start of 1998, PAP said.
PAP will be managed in line with the commerical code with one exception -- its first president and board will be chosen by the Treasury Minister on the approval of the Prime Minister.
The bill, now sent to the Senate, also envisions the creation of an advisory programme board, whose specific functions would later be set in the new PAP statute.
PAP said that its character would be "of a public press agency which among other things is obliged to publicise the stance of Poland's Sejm, Senate, President and government."
PAP will be subsidsed by the government until it is partially privatised, it said.
